title: Centre stalk ideal, normal-fibre algebra and polynomial degree subspaces
statement: Let $c:C\to X$ be a morphism of schemes and $z\in C$ [def-pc-scheme]. Set $R=\mathcal O_{X,c(z)}$ and let $I=\ker(\mathcal O_{X,c(z)}\to\mathcal O_{C,z})$; when $c$ is a closed immersion, this is the centre ideal in the stalk. Set $A=R/I$ [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient] and $k=\kappa(c(z))$ [def-weil-residue-field]. The canonical $A$-algebra structure on $k$ is the factorization of the residue map $R\to k$ through $A$ (the kernel $I$ is contained in the maximal ideal). Define the normal-fibre algebra $S=k\otimes_A\operatorname{gr}_I R$, using [def-weil-pbc-associated-graded-ring] and [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. For $n\ge0$, define its degree-$n$ subspace as the $k$-linear span of the elements $1\otimes\iota_n(a)$ for $a\in I^n/I^{n+1}$, where $\iota_n$ is the direct-sum inclusion. Separately, for any field $k$, commutative $k$-algebra $B$, family of $k$-submodules $(\mathcal B_j)_{j\ge0}$ of $B$, and integers $r,n\ge0$, define the degree-$n$ polynomial subspace in $B[T_1,\ldots,T_r]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] to be the $k$-linear span of the monomials $bT^d$ with $b\in\mathcal B_j$ and $j+\sum_i d_i=n$. These are explicit subspace constructions; no flatness, grading axiom, reducedness or near-point theorem is part of this definition.

source.place: Cossart--Jannsen--Saito, March 12 2009 preprint, section 2, Theorems 2.3 and 2.14, pp.29,36 (https://epub.uni-regensburg.de/13766/1/MP32.pdf): explicit centre-stalk and normal-cone fibre constructions and the total-degree polynomial grading used for the near-point statement. Existing Lean definitions in Sheaf.AlgebraicGeometry.HilbertSamuelNearNormalCone, lines 50--84.
